title: Odisha evacuates nearly 3 lakh people, 69 trains cancelled as Cyclone Akvan approaches with 110 kmph gusts - The New Indian Express

full_text:
Odisha has evacuated nearly three lakh people and deployed 423 rescue teams in vulnerable areas as it stepped up preparations ahead of severe cyclonic storm Akvan, which is likely to make landfall between Puri and Gopalpur on Friday afternoon, officials said.
The storm, the third to threaten the state in 24 days, changed its trajectory over the past 24 hours after initially being projected to make landfall along the Andhra Pradesh coast. The Odisha government has set up 9,341 cyclone shelters across potentially affected districts.
Special Relief Commissioner Rajesh P Patil said 2,98,676 people had been evacuated by Thursday evening and shifted to 2,523 relief camps.
"Akvan is now moving towards Odisha at 13 kmph and is likely to cross the coast around Friday afternoon," an India Meteorological Department (IMD) official said. The storm was around 410 km from Gopalpur and 470 km from Puri on Thursday evening.
IMD Director General Mrutyunjay Mohapatra said Akvan would cross the coast as a cyclonic storm, with wind speeds of 90-100 kmph. Southern Andhra Pradesh is expected to experience winds of 90-100 kmph, while Odisha is likely to see speeds of 70-80 kmph, he said. The system is expected to gradually weaken as it moves northwards through Odisha.
Iran suggested the name Akvan as part of the naming system for cyclones in the North Indian Ocean.
Chief Secretary Anu Garg said the state had deployed 60 teams of the Odisha Disaster Rapid Action Force (ODRAF), 14 teams of the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) and 131 teams of the Fire and Emergency Services. The government has also asked the Indian Coast Guard to keep its helicopters, vessels and other logistics ready for rescue and relief operations.
Arrangements are being made at cyclone shelters to provide cooked and dry food, essential medicines, drinking water, sanitary napkins and other facilities, Garg said.
Disaster Management Minister Suresh Pujari said the government had identified 941 landslide-prone locations across Ganjam, Gajapati, Kandhamal, Koraput and Malkangiri districts. Gajapati accounted for the highest number, with 211 such locations.
He said 10 people had died in landslides during the previous cyclone, Arnab. Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi, who reviewed the state's preparedness, stressed the need to maintain the government's zero-casualty mission.
The approaching storm has disrupted rail services. The East Coast Railway cancelled 41 trains and rescheduled 29 others, while the South Eastern Railway cancelled at least 28 express trains, mostly those bound for or passing through Puri on Friday.
Among the cancelled services are the Bhubaneswar-Visakhapatnam, Howrah-Puri and Tatanagar-Brahmapur Vande Bharat Express trains, as well as the Puri-Yesvantpur Garib Rath Express. The Howrah-Puri-Howrah Vande Bharat Express has also been cancelled for Friday.
Tourists have been prohibited from visiting coastal areas, including Gopalpur, Puri, Satapada and Chilika, while fishermen have been advised not to venture into the sea. The coastal and southern parts of Odisha have been receiving light to moderate rain since Wednesday night, with rainfall expected to intensify as the system approaches, Bhubaneswar Meteorological Centre Director Manorama Mohanty said.
Educational institutions in districts under red, orange and yellow warnings have been closed. Rescue teams have been deployed in Malkangiri, Koraput, Rayagada, Kalahandi, Gajapati, Ganjam, Kandhamal, Boudh, Puri, Nayagarh and Khurda districts.
The Gundicha Temple in Puri will remain closed to visitors from November 19 to 21. The 12th-century Jagannath Temple, however, will remain open, with daily rituals continuing as usual. Shree Jagannath Temple Administration Chief Administrator Arabinda Padhee urged devotees to plan their visits in accordance with weather advisories.
The Nandankanan Zoological Park and the adjoining State Botanical Garden in Bhubaneswar will remain closed on November 19 and 20. The Bhitarkanika National Park has been closed until November 21, while the Similipal Tiger Reserve will remain closed to visitors on November 20 and 21.
In Andhra Pradesh, the IMD has issued a red alert for Srikakulam and Vizianagaram districts, warning of extremely heavy rainfall at isolated places. An orange alert has been issued for Parvatipuram Manyam, Alluri Sitaramaraju and Anakapalli districts, while Kakinada is under a yellow alert.
The Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority has advised people in North Andhra to remain alert, urged farmers to take precautions during agricultural activities and asked fishermen not to venture into the sea.
Under the IMD's rainfall warning categories, a red alert indicates extremely heavy rainfall exceeding 20.44 cm in 24 hours. An orange alert denotes very heavy rainfall of 11.56 cm to 20.44 cm, while a yellow alert indicates heavy rainfall of 6.45 cm to 11.55 cm.
(With PTI inputs)

Cyclone Akvan's Track Shifts Towards Odisha
Severe Cyclonic Storm Akvan over the west-central Bay of Bengal has changed its projected path, bringing some relief to Andhra Pradesh after earlier forecasts indicated a greater risk of impact along the State's coastline.
According to the India Meteorological Department (IMD), the system was moving north-northwestwards and was expected to cross the North Andhra Pradesh–Yanam and South Odisha coasts between Narsapur and Puri, close to Gopalpur in Odisha, around noon on Friday, November 20.
The IMD's November 19 bulletin forecast maximum sustained wind speeds of 90–100 kmph, with gusts reaching 110 kmph, during the expected coastal crossing.
Red Alert Reduced to Three Andhra Pradesh Districts
The revised weather warning brought a reduction in the number of Andhra Pradesh districts under red alert.
For Thursday, November 19, the IMD retained its red warning for isolated extremely heavy rainfall in Srikakulam, Vizianagaram and Parvathipuram Manyam districts.
Earlier warnings had covered seven districts, including Kakinada, Visakhapatnam, Alluri Sitharama Raju and Anakapalli.
For Friday, November 20, the IMD forecast no red alert for Andhra Pradesh. However, an orange alert for heavy to very heavy rainfall remained for Srikakulam and Parvathipuram Manyam districts. Isolated heavy rainfall was also possible in parts of Visakhapatnam, Vizianagaram and Alluri Sitharama Raju districts.
Coastal Districts Remain on Alert
Although the expected landfall shifted towards Odisha, northern coastal Andhra Pradesh continued to face the possibility of strong winds, heavy rainfall and rough sea conditions.
The IMD reported that gales of 60–80 kmph had prevailed at isolated places along coastal Andhra Pradesh and Yanam on Thursday, with wind intensity expected to increase on Friday.
District administrations in Srikakulam and Vizianagaram were reviewing preparedness in vulnerable areas, particularly villages near the Andhra Pradesh–Odisha border. Disaster response teams were also being prepared for possible rescue and relief operations.
Odisha Steps Up Cyclone Preparations
With the projected landfall moving closer to Odisha, the neighbouring State intensified its preparedness measures.
According to officials cited by The New Indian Express, nearly three lakh people had been evacuated in Odisha by Thursday evening, and 423 rescue teams had been deployed. The State had also arranged thousands of cyclone shelters.
The cyclone's revised trajectory has therefore shifted the focus of the immediate landfall preparations towards southern Odisha, while northern Andhra Pradesh remains under rainfall and wind warnings.
Residents in affected coastal districts should continue following official IMD and district administration advisories, as cyclone tracks and rainfall forecasts can change.
